title: Staged checkpoints for config apply with cost-aware throttles and auditable reconciliation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Config changes that tune batching, KV caching, and kernel selection materially affect cost and latency. We need an automated apply flow that (1) reduces blast radius for economic regressions, (2) supports safe, auditable rollback, and (3) reconciles control-plane view with runtime state when partial applies or failures occur.

Goal: Implement a staged checkpointing apply pipeline with cost-aware throttles (rate-limited percentage ramp-ups tied to observed unit cost), deterministic reconciliation steps, and an auditable event stream for post-mortems. This will be used for both host-level config (routing, throttles, autoscale settings) and model-serving tuning (batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, quantization profile toggles).

Scope & deliverables:
- Checkpointed apply engine: snapshot current config, compute delta, and produce N checkpoints (stages) with traffic split and slow ramp options.
- Cost-aware throttle controller: a feedback loop that pauses or steps back a stage when token-unit cost, p95 latency, or error rate exceeds configured thresholds.
- Reconciliation daemon: idempotent loop that compares desired config store, runtime-applied state, and recent events; attempts safe reapply up to retry budget and surfaces unreconciled diffs to the control plane.
- Audit trail & explainability UI: store per-stage metrics and decisions (why stage advanced/paused/rolled back) in the Console timeline and in a durable event log.
- Canary/Shadow test harness: small-traffic simulated workloads to verify cost delta before full rollout.

Success criteria:
- Can apply a config that increases default batching by 2x with automated rollout completing without manual intervention in >= 90% of runs across staging clusters.
- Automatic pause/rollback triggers on cost increase > 15% or p95 latency degradation > 20%.
- Reconciler converges (< 3 attempts) for transient failures caused by node restarts or partial apply errors.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Use staged percentage ramps (1%, 5%, 20%, 80%, 100%) rather than fixed time windows so rollout adapts to traffic. Trade-off: more complex metric evaluation vs safer economics.
- Cost signal will be derived from token-unit cost computed from token counts + local billing metrics instead of cloud billing (lag). Rationale: lower latency for decisioning; risk: short-term noise — mitigated by smoothing over 1 minute moving window.
- Reconciler will prefer natively supported control-plane APIs for apply/revert to ensure idempotency rather than brute-forcing manual changes.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec & API (week 1): define checkpoint manifest, stage contract, and events. Write PRD and console wireframe.
2) Checkpoint engine (week 2–3): implement snapshot/diff, stage plan generation, and persistent checkpoint store.
3) Throttle controller (week 3–4): implement cost/latency/error monitors, smoothing windows, and decision logic.
4) Reconciler (week 4–5): implement compare/apply loop with exponential backoff and retry budget.
5) Telemetry & UI (week 5): add per-stage metrics, Console timeline, and runbook links.
6) E2E tests & rollout (week 6): integration tests with canary harness, simulate failure modes, and pilot on a subset of accounts.

Monitoring & metrics to watch:
- token_unit_cost_delta_pct (per-stage)
- p95_latency_delta_pct (per-stage)
- error_rate_change (per-stage)
- reconcile_attempts_per_apply
- stage_duration_seconds
- rollback_rate_by_change_type

Runbook excerpts for automated pause/rollback:
- Pause stage if token_unit_cost_delta_pct > 15% OR p95_latency_delta_pct > 20% sustained for 2 consecutive windows (1min each).
- Rollback immediately if error_rate_change > 5% AND request error rate > 0.5% absolute.
- If reconciler fails > 3 attempts, escalate to oncall and mark change as Blocked; capture diagnostic artifacts for postmortem.

Testing matrix:
- Unit tests for checkpoint diff/apply/revert semantics.
- Integration tests that inject synthetic workload and assert staged progression or pause/rollback triggers.
- Fault injection tests: node restart during stage, partial API failures, and event duplication.
- Load soak: run 48h canary with new batching settings and compare unit cost/latency to baseline.

Rollout plan:
- Pilot on internal staging clusters + 5 low-SLA customers (opt-in) for 2 weeks.
- Expand to 20% of non-SLA orgs if stable.
- Default enable for all orgs after 6 weeks & postmortem signoff.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Threshold tuning: should thresholds be static or learned per-customer baseline? (Follow-up spike: ML-based baseline detection in Q3).
- How to present 'reason for rollback' succinctly in Console for non-technical PMs? (Design suggestion: color-coded root cause + quick link to metrics).
- Should we allow manual stage jump (advance to 100%) in the UI and require additional guardrails? (Proposed: restrict to admins and emit a signed acknowledgement).
